title: AI Quiz for First-Year Students
description: An introductory quiz for first-year students covering fundamental AI concepts, designed to build early interest in the field.
highlights: Builds early interest in AI before deeper vertical events

title: Vibe Coding Workshop
description: A practical workshop introducing AI-assisted software development using modern tools.

title: Robotics & IoT Learning Workshops
description: Hands-on workshops covering Arduino, ESP32, sensors, motors, wireless communication, and rapid prototyping, with opportunities for expert talks from industry and academia.

title: Portfolio Wars
description: Each team gets a fixed amount of virtual funds to invest across trending products, sectors, or markets. Teams research the trends they invest in, build a case for why each pick will perform well, and predict their eventual profit or loss.
highlights: Virtual seed fund allocated to every team
Research across tech, consumer products, startups & markets
Live rebalancing rounds based on simulated market events
Profit/loss prediction backed by written reasoning
Final presentation defending the investment thesis

title: CampusQuest
description: A campus-wide collaborative event that brings together students from various departments to solve logic, strategy, and puzzle-based challenges while encouraging teamwork and networking.

title: The Forensic Hypothesis (The Murder Mystery)
description: A high-energy analytical challenge where students step into the shoes of investigators to solve a simulated crime scene using core research frameworks instead of guesswork.
highlights: Interactive case files: raw evidence, witness statements & psychological profiles to analyze

title: Ultimate Funathlon
description: A team-based sports festival inspired by The Amazing Race and Survivor. Participants compete across multiple zones featuring speed, teamwork, strategy, and precision challenges. The highest-scoring team is crowned the Labyrinth Champions.

title: Robotics & IoT Learning Workshops (Round 2)
description: A further round of hands-on workshops covering Arduino, ESP32, sensors, motors, wireless communication, and rapid prototyping, with expert talks from industry and academia.

title: Asian Parliamentary Conference: Diplomacy & Deliberation
description: A one-day Model United Nations (PreMUN) conference introducing participants to the fundamentals of diplomacy, international relations, and policy-making, conducted through a single committee under a common agenda.

title: Workshop on Explainable AI (XAI)
description: A hands-on session helping students understand interpretable and trustworthy AI models, and why explainability matters in real-world deployment.
highlights: Hands-on with real tools (SHAP, LIME) rather than just theory

title: Datathon
description: A high-energy, 24-48 hour challenge where teams are handed a raw, messy real-world dataset and tasked with turning it into insights, a story, and a compelling dashboard - all under time pressure.
highlights: Focus on asking the right questions, not just writing code
Showcase event for Labyrinth's data analytics vertical

title: AI-Based Mini Hackathon
description: A short-format hackathon where teams build AI-based solutions to a given real-world problem statement within a fixed time window.
highlights: Highest energy, most visible event of the vertical

title: Workshop on MLOps
description: Covers the practical AI development lifecycle, including model deployment, monitoring, and versioning, aimed at bridging the gap between building and shipping models.
highlights: Bridges the build vs ship gap

title: UPSC Training Session
description: An introductory session providing insights into UPSC preparation, examination strategy, and opportunities in public service.

title: Project Showcase
description: Students present their AI and machine learning projects to faculty and peers, demonstrating their work and receiving feedback.
highlights: Capstone event for real AI/ML projects
Judging panel + certificates for a formal, recognition-driven feel
Works well as a semester closer

title: CODESPRINT-A: Five-Day Build, One Hour at a Time
description: A 5-day guided development sprint where pairs of students commit to one hour of coding per day to build, refine, and ship a complete, functional project. Promotes sustained skill-building and structured daily progress over traditional all-night hackathons.
dateLabel: September 2026 - exact date to be decided
highlights: Mentorship pairings for technical collaboration & cross-cohort mentorship
Disciplined format: 5 consecutive days, 1 hour daily, one shipped project
Progress tracked on a leaderboard across 4 evaluation checkpoints
Judging on code understanding, execution quality, consistency & SDG alignment
Final showcase with live demos and team Q&A

title: Digital Literacy Outreach Program
description: A collaborative outreach initiative with CSA to provide children under the Child Sponsorship Program and students from government schools with basic computer skills, internet awareness, digital tools, and online safety through interactive, hands-on sessions.
highlights: Introduction to internet and web browsing
Targeted at CSP children & government school students

title: RoundTable
description: A 2-day conference with two committees: the Indian Committee and the United Nations (UN) Committee.

title: Impact Analytics Challenge
description: Unlike generic student hackathons, this gives participants the chance to work with real stakeholders, understand real-world constraints, and deliver practical insights that create measurable impact. The partner organization sits on the judging panel and picks a most useful winner.
highlights: 2-3 partner organizations identified before the event
Each partner presents a 5-minute overview of their challenge
Teams select a partner and receive an anonymized dataset
Teams build dashboards, reports or recommendations
Winning solutions handed over for implementation

title: AI Short Film Challenge
description: A creative AI competition where teams produce a short film using AI-powered tools.

title: Code vs AI Challenge
description: Participants build a web application under two different conditions, comparing hand-written development against AI-assisted development.

title: Line Gate
description: A practical robotics event where participants design, build, and program an autonomous line-following robot, introducing concepts such as sensor calibration, motor control, and embedded programming.
